flags.title: A published pick cites a URL outside the official allow-list
An independent official line disagrees with the published pick for 1079588
flags.detail: Astralis vs MIBR (Stake Pulse Beat III, 2026-10-16T14:00:00Z): the site picks MIBR from Polymarket via its market rung ([48.5, 51.5]%, observed 2026-10-16T08:18:29Z), while Bovada (['1.833333', '1.909091'], overround 1.069264, observed 2026-10-16T08:20:41Z) de-vigs to Astralis ([51.0, 49.0]%). The two official sources are 2.51 percentage points apart, which is enough to flip the pick on a near-even match. Both are linked; neither was overridden, and no third opinion was invented to break the tie.

flags.title: Picks are published on margins smaller than the spread of their own source
flags.detail: The origination ladder publishes a pick for every fixture it can price and has no minimum-edge threshold (the deployed snapshot reports no_edge=0). 2 resolved fixture(s) are decided by less than 5 percentage points: 1079588 Astralis vs MIBR [48.5, 51.5]%; 1079588 Astralis vs MIBR [48.5, 51.5]%. These are arithmetically correct and every one replays from its cited source, but a reader on a phone cannot distinguish a 1.5-point margin from a strong favourite. Reported as a presentation irregularity, not a data error.

Independently re-read from the archived book, this confirms the site's rejection rather than contradicting it. No probability is inferred.

flags.title: source_outcomes is published in market order while probabilities is in team order
flags.detail: scripts/domain.py::market_analysis aligns `quotes` and `probabilities` to the fixture's team order but records `source_outcomes` in the market's own order. 2 published row(s) therefore carry the two arrays in opposite orders (1081497, 1080289). Every one was verified correct against Polymarket's own archived prices, so no published probability is wrong; but a reviewer comparing the two arrays positionally would invert the favourite. Nothing is rendered from `source_outcomes` on any page today.
